summary: Markets opened lower Thursday as oil prices surged above $104 and Treasury yields hit fresh multi-decade highs, reigniting inflation concerns and prompting a defensive tilt across equities. The S&P 500 fell 0.3% while the Nasdaq dropped 1.3% following a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualized revenue fell short of expectations, triggering a selloff in chipmakers. Meanwhile, Fed minutes released Wednesday showed most officials view another rate hike by year-end as appropriate, though weak September payrolls—just 29,000 jobs added versus 84,000 expected—have traders pricing only a 20% chance of an October hike. Crypto markets tumbled in tandem, with Bitcoin sliding below $83,000 after U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded their largest single-day outflow since June, hemorrhaging $485 million on October 7. BlackRock's IBIT led redemptions at $207.7 million, erasing October's early gains and signaling waning institutional appetite amid elevated yields and a firmer dollar.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs See Largest Outflow Since June at $485M
signals.desc: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $485 million on October 7, led by BlackRock's IBIT with $207.7 million in withdrawals, turning monthly flows negative and pressuring BTC below $83,000.

signals.title: Fed Minutes Signal December Rate Hike Likely Despite Weak Jobs Data
signals.desc: FOMC minutes showed most officials expect another quarter-point hike by year-end, though September payrolls of only 29,000 have reduced October hike odds to 20%, keeping pressure on risk assets.

signals.title: Oil Surges Above $104, Treasury Yields Hit 24-Year Highs
signals.desc: Brent crude climbed above $104 while the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.34%, the highest since 2002, reviving stagflation fears and weighing on equities and crypto.

signals.title: Chipmakers Sink on OpenAI Revenue Miss Report
signals.desc: Financial Times reported OpenAI's annualized revenue is $20 billion below expectations, sending semiconductor stocks down 3% and dragging the Nasdaq 100 down 1.3% to session lows.

signals.title: Megacap Earnings Season Set to Begin Late October
signals.desc: Microsoft and Alphabet report October 27, followed by Meta, Apple, Amazon, and Tesla on October 28, with AI capex and revenue monetization the key focus for investors.

verdict: Risk-off tone dominates as surging oil and yields collide with Fed hawkishness and crypto ETF outflows, pressuring equities and digital assets into the CPI print on October 14.
